I want to start Phase 5. Here is a quick outcome of some brainstorming. Just internalize and wait for my next prompt for details. Not expecting any sustantive response to this prompt

___________________
✅ Agreed / decided 

Build the agent-platform capabilities once as a shared, reusable layer, pilot on mcp-agent (Phase 1 refill-triage agent — it already has the conversational shape), then carry to the Phase 2 claims stack.
Phase 5 is It's its own phase, NOT folded into Phase 2. Reasons settled: the "Phase 2 is cloud-ready" premise contradicts our documented cloud-delivery gap; this work is cloud-agnostic anyway; the conversational surface you described is Phase 1's agent; reopening a completed phase repeats the status-truthfulness problem; these are shared-platform capabilities.
Agent is becoming clinician-facing → the heavy tier (policy + judge, M6) is justified.
PHI-off-third-party = a future business rule → build the provider seam now, keep Anthropic the only live backend for now; target providers are Anthropic + Llama + DeepSeek.
Provider abstraction = two adapters only: Anthropic (native) + OpenAI-compatible (covers Llama, DeepSeek, Ollama, vLLM, and hosted endpoints). Llama-vs-DeepSeek becomes config, not code.
Output safety is a MUST: tool-with-enum-output + code validation + fail-closed to REVIEW.
policy.md into the system prompt — NOT RAG. RAG only for a genuine knowledge base, kept separate.
LLM-as-judge only for "important" responses, checking soft qualities; code enforces hard invariants.
Build order (by dependency, not your 1–5): M1 enum-gate → M2 OTel → M3 memory/context+session store → M4 deploy resilience+cost alerts → M5 provider abstraction → M6 policy+knowledge+judge. Minimal cut = M1 + M2.
Cheap Llama/DeepSeek testing: stub OpenAI-compatible server ($0 CI) / Ollama local ($0, weak — good adversary for the enum gate) / hosted OpenAI-compatible like DeepSeek API/OpenRouter/Groq (pennies, real quality).

🟡 Open issues to be brainstormed

Exact enum set for the pilot surface (dispense / review / don't-dispense is the shape; confirm the set and how REVIEW is the fail-closed sink).
Definition of an "important" response that triggers the judge.
Session-store tech (Redis vs Postgres — tie to existing infra) and where the shared platform layer lives (new agent-platform/ package vs in-place refactor).
Memory token-budget numbers — deliberately deferred until M2 metrics exist so they're set from data, not guessed.
Conversational transport — CLI REPL today; is the clinician surface a web/chat UI or API? (drives streaming + session design).
M6 RAG corpus (formulary? drug info?) or defer RAG entirely.
Phase number/name — a docs/phase5/ readiness-assessment already exists; confirm this is Phase 5 vs Phase 6, and whether the observability slice formally closes Phase 2's unbuilt R15.
_______________________________________

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

---
name: phase5-agent-hardening
description: "Phase 5 scoping — agent-tier productionization (memory, observability, multi-provider, follow-ups, output-safety); planning only, not yet built."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: bebf7ac2-4f1b-4a70-8685-440da76db7e1
  modified: 2026-08-02T02:50:37.886Z
---

Planning an **agent-platform-hardening** phase (naturally Phase 5 — Phase 4/epic-emulator is
done; `docs/phase5/` holds only a readiness-assessment; branch `docs/phase5-readiness-assessment`).
Read-only/brainstorm stage — no code, no repo writes yet. User will ask for a **comprehensive
report after several milestones land** — prepare topic-4 down to code snippets especially.

Five topics the work must cover (user's numbering):
1. **Memory** — separate three axes: per-conversation token budget (cap+compact, not "autoscale"),
   concurrent-session count (real autoscale = compute), cross-session persistence store. Note:
   `MAX_TOKENS=1024` in [agent.py] is the OUTPUT cap, not memory. No memory mgmt exists today.
2. **Deploy + observability** — bounded queue + deadline (avoid queue-of-doom) as client-side
   token-bucket in front of the rate-limited/paid Anthropic API; Grafana needs metrics pipeline
   first; rate/cost ALERTS not auto-shed (clinical). 
3. **Observability (full)** — OTel: run=trace, model/tool calls=spans, `gen_ai.*` attributes,
   propagate traceID INTO claims/triage/fhir, PHI-redaction of span attrs. Strongest/most natural ask.
4. **Follow-ups + multi-model** — Meta=Llama, DeepSeek(V3/R1). Self-host via vLLM/TGI/Ollama,
   OpenAI-compatible. Real driver = PHI-off-third-party (future business rule), NOT cost.
5. **Output safety** — policy.md into system prompt (NOT RAG — rules always apply); RAG only for a
   real knowledge base; multi-model LLM-as-judge on "important" responses (code enforces hard rules,
   judge checks soft); MUST limit final answer to N enums via tool-with-enum-output + code validation
   + fail-closed to REVIEW. This is the fail-closed thesis applied to agent OUTPUT.

Proposed build order (dependency, not user's 1-5): M1 enum-gate (cheap, first, safety) · M2 OTel
foundation (the lens) · M3 memory/context+session store · M4 deploy resilience+cost alerts+Grafana ·
M5 provider abstraction (2 adapters only: Anthropic native + OpenAI-compatible covering Llama/DeepSeek/
Ollama/vLLM/hosted) · M6 policy+knowledge+judge. Minimal cut = M1+M2.

Cheap testing of Llama/DeepSeek: stub OpenAI-compatible server ($0 CI) / Ollama local ($0, weak — good
adversary for enum gate) / hosted OpenAI-compat like DeepSeek API/OpenRouter/Groq (pennies, real quality).

**KEY UNRESOLVED SCOPING DEBATE:** User proposed folding all this into **Phase 2** (adding milestones
to it), reasoning Phase 2 is "more cloud-ready." I pushed back hard: (a) that premise contradicts our
own [[cloud-delivery-gap]] docs — Phase 2 has cloud *design* but no root Terraform, not deployable;
(b) cloud-readiness is irrelevant — this work is local/cloud-agnostic; (c) the clinician-facing
conversational surface the user describes (patient/med disambiguation, dispense/review/hold) is the
**Phase 1 mcp-agent (refill triage)**, NOT Phase 2's claims-agent (which only *explains* adjudication);
(d) reopening completed-and-tagged Phase 2 repeats the status-truthfulness problem the reviewer caught;
(e) these are SHARED-PLATFORM capabilities (build once, reuse across agents like client/clinical).
Counter-proposal: own phase + shared reusable layer + scope first pass to ONE agent + defer Phase 3/4
explicitly. Observability slice arguably finishes Phase 2's unbuilt **R15**.
**OPEN QUESTION to user:** which agent is the clinician surface — (a) mcp-agent/Phase1, (b) new/evolved
claims-agent/Phase2, (c) both, platform-first then pilot on (a). My read: (c) with (a) as pilot.

Confirmed by user: agent IS becoming clinician-facing (so M6 judge/policy justified); PHI-off-3rd-party
is a FUTURE rule so build the provider SEAM now but keep Anthropic the only live backend.

Agent is hardcoded to Anthropic today (`import anthropic`, MODEL="claude-sonnet-4-5", no provider seam).
Multi-turn already works in `interactive_mode` REPL (grows `messages`); single-shot `--query` does not persist.

Here is a handoff document. Just internalize without sustantive response. I will feed you some more info before soliticing ananysis and critique:

_________________

# Phase 5 Handoff — Agent Platform Hardening (fhir-agent)

> Paste this whole document as the first message of a fresh Claude Code session to
> bootstrap Phase 5. It captures brainstorming already done; **decisions marked ✅ are
> settled — implement them, don't re-open them.** Items marked 🟡 are for you to resolve
> with me early.

## 0. How to use this doc
You are resuming a multi-session effort on the `fhir-agent` project. Phases 1–4 are built
and merged. This document defines **Phase 5: Agent Platform Hardening**. Start by reading
`CLAUDE.md`, `docs/README.md`, and the memory file `phase5-agent-hardening.md`, then confirm
the 🟡 open questions in §8 with me before writing milestone docs.

## 1. Project orientation (what fhir-agent is)
An agentic healthcare platform. A clinician asks a natural-language question; an LLM/agent
layer fetches FHIR data and returns a structured recommendation. Deterministic services
decide; the agent orchestrates and explains. Two guiding sentences the whole codebase obeys:
- **AI explains and orchestrates; deterministic services decide.**
- **The legacy core is wrapped, not rewritten.**

Relevant components:
- `mcp-agent/` (Python) — **Phase 1** refill-risk-triage agent. Anthropic tool-use CLI. This
  is the **pilot target** for Phase 5 (it already has the conversational shape).
- `claims-agent/` (Python) — **Phase 2** explanation agent; explains adjudication decisions,
  non-authoritative. The **second target**, later.
- `claims-service/`, `rxclaim-emulator/`, `triage-service/`, `fhir-service/`, `epic-emulator/`,
  gateway (Kong) — the deterministic tiers the agents call.
- Docs live in `docs/` (guides) and `docs/phase2../phase4/` (per-phase). Decisions index:
  `docs/phase2/decisions.md`.

Working rules (from `CLAUDE.md`): two git worktrees; **never commit to `main`** — always a
feature branch + PR; never self-merge. Treat claims/clinical data as **PHI**.

## 2. What Phase 5 is
Harden the **agent tier** to the same standard as the decision tier, and turn the pilot agent
into a **clinician-facing conversational surface**. Built as a **shared, reusable platform
layer** (like `client/clinical` is shared) and **applied to one agent first**.

**Scope decision (✅):** Option (c) — build the platform once, **pilot on `mcp-agent`** (Phase 1
refill agent), then carry to the Phase 2 claims stack. **Explicitly defer Phase 3/4 agents.**
This is a **new phase, not an extension of Phase 2.** (Rationale in §7.)

## 3. The five topics this phase covers
1. **Memory** — short-term (the in-context transcript) vs long-term (cross-session store).
   Three distinct axes, do not conflate: per-conversation token budget (cap + compact),
   concurrent-session count (the thing that actually autoscales = compute), cross-session
   persistence store. `MAX_TOKENS=1024` today is the **output** cap, not memory. **Clinical
   rule: re-fetch from FHIR, never act on recalled state** (data changes; stale recall = the
   fail-open bug in disguise).
2. **Deployment + observability tie-in** — bounded queue + per-request deadline (avoid the
   "queue of doom"); the "queue" is really a **client-side token-bucket / concurrency limiter
   in front of the rate-limited, paid LLM API** (that, not local CPU/RAM, is the bottleneck);
   rate/cost **alerts, not auto-shed** (clinical — never silently drop a care request);
   Grafana needs a metrics pipeline **first** (instrument → Prometheus → dashboard).
3. **Observability (full)** — OTel. **A trace = one agent run; spans = reasoning steps** (each
   model call, each tool call). Use OTel `gen_ai.*` semantic conventions. **Propagate the
   traceID *through* tool calls into claims/triage/fhir** so one trace spans cognition →
   deterministic services. **PHI-redact span attributes** (that's where PHI leaks).
4. **Follow-ups + multi-model** — Meta's model = **Llama**; also **DeepSeek** (V3 general, R1
   reasoning). Self-host via vLLM/TGI/Ollama, all OpenAI-compatible. **Driver = PHI residency
   (future rule), NOT cost.** Multi-turn already works in the REPL; the hard part of multi-model
   is normalizing tool-calling + translating conversation history across providers.
5. **Output safety** — `policy.md` of NL rules loaded into the system prompt (**NOT RAG** — the
   rules always apply). RAG only for a real **knowledge base** (separate concern). **Limit the
   final answer to N enum options** via tool-with-enum-output **+** code validation **+**
   **fail-closed to REVIEW** if the model returns anything else. Optional **LLM-as-judge** on
   "important" responses for *soft* qualities only (groundedness, tone, PHI leak) — **code
   enforces hard invariants, never a judge model.** A narrow output surface is also the
   strongest control against "answers the LLM shouldn't give."

## 4. Milestones (✅ order is by dependency, not by topic number)
| M | Milestone | Topic | Why here | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **M1** | Output contract & enum gate (tool-with-enum-output; validate in code; fail-closed to REVIEW; narrow the surface) | 5 | Cheap, independent, highest safety value; extends the fail-closed thesis. Do first. | S |
| **M2** | Observability foundation (OTel traces/spans; `gen_ai.*`; traceID propagated into services; PHI redaction) | 3 | The lens. Underpins tuning M3, seeing M4, evaluating M6. | M |
| **M3** | Context & memory mgmt (explicit token budget + documented rationale; compaction at threshold; externalized session store; re-fetch-don't-recall) | 1, 4 | Needs M2's token metrics to set limits honestly. | M |
| **M4** | Deploy resilience & cost control (bounded queue + deadline; token-bucket/concurrency limiter; rate/cost alerts; Grafana dashboards) | 2 | Needs M2 metrics + M3 session model. | M |
| **M5** | Provider abstraction + cross-model follow-ups (2 adapters: Anthropic native + OpenAI-compatible; history translation) | 4 | Backbone for M6; capture follow-up code detail here for the report. | L |
| **M6** | Policy + knowledge + judge (`policy.md` into system prompt; optional RAG knowledge base; LLM-as-judge on important responses) | 5 | Sits on M1 + M5; heaviest; justified because the agent is clinician-facing. | L |

**Minimal viable cut:** M1 + M2 (closes the biggest agent-tier safety gap and gives you eyes).

## 5. Key technical decisions (✅ settled)
- **Provider layer = exactly two adapters:** `Anthropic` (native tool-use) and
  `OpenAI-compatible` (one adapter covering Llama, DeepSeek, Ollama, vLLM, and hosted
  endpoints like DeepSeek API / OpenRouter / Together / Groq). Llama vs DeepSeek = base-URL +
  model-name **config**, not new code. **Anthropic stays the only live backend for now**; the
  others exist to prove the seam.
- **Enum gate:** structured output (tool with enum) constrains *shape*; **still validate in
  code**; **fail closed to REVIEW** on anything off-contract. This is the project's fail-closed
  safety thesis applied to the agent's *output*.
- **Rules vs knowledge:** behavioral rules → `policy.md` into the system prompt (always apply,
  no retrieval). Knowledge base → RAG (retrieve relevant subset). **Do not use RAG for rules.**
- **Judge:** reserve for "important" responses; checks soft qualities; never the enforcer of
  anything code can enforce.
- **Cheap multi-model testing:** stub OpenAI-compatible server ($0 CI, same JDK-HttpServer /
  Python-http stub pattern already used in `HttpTriageClientTest`) · Ollama local ($0, weak —
  a *good adversary* for the enum gate) · hosted OpenAI-compatible (pennies, real quality).

## 6. Current code facts (verify before relying — memory may be stale)
- `mcp-agent/src/agent/agent.py`: hardcoded to Anthropic (`import anthropic`,
  `MODEL="claude-sonnet-4-5"`, `MAX_TOKENS=1024`), a `SYSTEM_PROMPT` constant, an agent loop
  `run_query(client, user_input, messages) -> (final_text, messages)`, and an
  `interactive_mode` REPL that **persists `messages` across turns** (follow-ups work in the
  REPL). The single-shot `--query` path does **not** persist across invocations.
- `mcp-agent/src/agent/tools.py`: tool definitions + `execute_tool`.
- **No observability anywhere** (no OTel/metrics/tracing) — clean slate.
- `claims-agent` has a `--no-llm` deterministic mode — useful as a live oracle for drift
  detection.

## 7. Why its own phase, not folded into Phase 2 (✅ — do not re-open)
- "Phase 2 is more cloud-ready" is **false per our own docs** — Phase 2 has cloud *design* but
  **no root Terraform module / not deployable** (the documented cloud-delivery gap).
- Cloud-readiness is **irrelevant** — all of this is built and tested locally, cloud-agnostic.
- The clinician conversational surface described (patient/med disambiguation, dispense/review/
  hold) is **Phase 1's `mcp-agent`**, not Phase 2's claims *explainer*.
- Reopening a completed, tagged, "done" Phase 2 repeats a status-truthfulness problem.
- These are **shared-platform capabilities** — build once, reuse across agents.
- Honest carve-out: the **observability slice may legitimately close Phase 2's unbuilt R15**,
  but do it *from the shared layer*, not by reopening Phase 2's M0–M7.

## 8. Open questions to resolve with the user first (🟡)
1. Exact **enum set** for the pilot surface and how REVIEW is the fail-closed sink.
2. Definition of an **"important" response** that triggers the judge.
3. **Session-store tech** (Redis vs Postgres) and **where the shared layer lives**
   (`agent-platform/` package vs in-place refactor).
4. **Memory token-budget numbers** — deliberately deferred until M2 metrics exist.
5. **Conversational transport** — CLI REPL today; web/chat UI or API? (drives streaming +
   session design).
6. **M6 RAG corpus** scope, or defer RAG.
7. **Phase number/name** confirmation (a `docs/phase5/` readiness-assessment already exists).

## 9. Cross-cutting principles (apply to every milestone)
- **Fail-closed everywhere, consistently** (enum → REVIEW; queue deadline → fail closed; judge
  disagreement → hold for human; memory → re-fetch not recall).
- **Deterministic code decides; the LLM orchestrates and explains** — the project thesis; the
  enum gate *is* this thesis applied to agent output.
- **PHI-safe is a driver, not just a constraint** (redact spans; don't persist raw PHI;
  self-hosting is a PHI *win*, which is why it's on the roadmap at all).
- **Observability first** — you can't tune memory, see deployment issues, or evaluate
  multi-model quality without M2.
- **The agent is non-authoritative** — it never decides anything clinical/financial.

## 10. Relevant existing memories to check
- `llm-tool-schema-oneof-unreliable` — **directly relevant to M1 and M5**: live Claude
  stringifies `oneOf`-typed nested tool params instead of emitting a native object. Flatten
  tool schemas; validate cross-field rules downstream. Expect worse behavior from small
  self-hosted models — another reason the enum gate validates in code.
- `pytest-test-filename-collision` — same-named `test_*.py` in different packages collide under
  this repo's `import-mode=importlib`. Check before adding any test file.
- `secret-values-never-print` — never echo secret values; redact in output. Extends naturally
  to PHI redaction in traces/logs.

## 11. A comprehensive report is owed (do not forget)
After the milestones (or several) land, the user will ask for a **comprehensive report**. It
must include, at minimum:
- **Follow-ups down to code snippets** — the `run_query(messages)→messages` mechanics, REPL
  persistence, the single-shot gap, and how each enhancement (session store, context
  compaction, tool-result compaction, re-fetch-don't-recall) changes specific lines; plus how
  the provider adapter translates conversation history for Llama/DeepSeek.
- **Memory sizing** — where each limit is set, the rationale for each number, and the autoscale
  path (per-conversation compaction vs session-count scaling vs store).
- **Observability** — the actual Grafana panels and the end-to-end trace/span/attribute schema.
Produce it *after* implementation, grounded in real code and real metrics — not predicted.

session and is the canonical source for scope, milestones §4, decisions §5, code facts §6, open
questions §8, cross-cutting principles §9, and the report spec §11 — treat that doc's content as
settled/authoritative over any summary here if they ever conflict.

## The 5 topics (fixed numbering, referenced throughout by number)

1. **Memory** — token budget/compaction, session-count autoscale, cross-session store,
   re-fetch-don't-recall.
2. **Deployment + observability tie-in** — bounded queue/deadline, token-bucket/concurrency
   limiter in front of the paid LLM API, rate/cost alerts (not auto-shed), Grafana dashboards.
3. **Observability (full)** — OTel: trace=one agent run, spans=reasoning steps, `gen_ai.*`
   attributes, traceID propagated into claims/triage/fhir, PHI-redacted span attributes.
4. **Follow-ups + multi-model** — provider abstraction (Anthropic native + OpenAI-compatible),
   Llama/DeepSeek as config not code, conversation-history translation across providers.
5. **Output safety** — policy.md into system prompt (NOT RAG), tool-with-enum-output + code
   validation + fail-closed to REVIEW, LLM-as-judge on "important" responses for soft qualities
   only (code enforces hard invariants).

## Decided (✅ per handoff doc — do not re-open)

- Phase 5 is its OWN phase, NOT folded into Phase 2 (see [[cloud-delivery-gap]]; rationale in
  handoff §7).
- Strategy: build the platform once as a shared reusable layer, **pilot on `mcp-agent`** (Phase 1
  refill-triage agent), then carry to Phase 2's claims stack. Phase 3/4 agents explicitly deferred.
- Agent is becoming clinician-facing → M6 (policy+judge) is justified.
- PHI-off-third-party = a FUTURE rule → build the provider seam now, **Anthropic stays the only
  live backend**. Target providers when activated: Anthropic + Llama + DeepSeek.
- Provider abstraction = exactly **two adapters**: Anthropic (native) + OpenAI-compatible (covers
  Llama, DeepSeek, Ollama, vLLM, hosted endpoints). Model choice becomes config, not code.
- Output safety is a MUST: enum-gate + code validation + fail-closed to REVIEW.
- Rules → policy.md in system prompt; RAG reserved only for a genuine knowledge base.
- Milestone order (dependency, not topic-number order): **M1 enum-gate (topic 5) → M2 OTel
  foundation (topic 3) → M3 memory/context+session store (topics 1,4) → M4 deploy resilience+cost
  alerts (topic 2) → M5 provider abstraction (topic 4) → M6 policy+knowledge+judge (topic 5).**
  Minimal viable cut = M1 + M2.
- Cheap Llama/DeepSeek testing: stub OpenAI-compatible server ($0 CI) / Ollama local ($0, weak
  adversary for enum gate) / hosted OpenAI-compatible — DeepSeek API/OpenRouter/Groq (pennies).

## Open issues (🟡 handoff §8 — resolve with user before milestone docs)

1. Exact enum set for the pilot surface + how REVIEW is the fail-closed sink.
2. Definition of an "important" response that triggers the judge.
3. Session-store tech (Redis vs Postgres) and where the shared layer lives (`agent-platform/`
   package vs in-place refactor).
4. Memory token-budget numbers — deferred until M2 metrics exist.
5. Conversational transport — CLI REPL today; web/chat UI or API? (drives streaming/session design).
6. M6 RAG corpus scope, or defer RAG.
7. Phase number/name confirmation; whether the observability slice formally closes Phase 2's
   unbuilt R15.

## Comprehensive report obligation (handoff §11 — owed after milestones land, not before)

Must include, mapped to topic numbers above:
- **Topic 4** down to code snippets: `run_query(messages)→messages` mechanics, REPL persistence,
  the single-shot `--query` gap, and how each enhancement (session store, context compaction,
  tool-result compaction, re-fetch-don't-recall) changes specific lines; plus how the provider
  adapter translates conversation history for Llama/DeepSeek.
- **Topic 1**: where each memory limit is set, the rationale for each number, and the autoscale
  path (per-conversation compaction vs session-count scaling vs persistence store).
- **Topics 2 & 3**: the actual Grafana panels and the end-to-end trace/span/attribute schema.
Must be grounded in real code and real metrics after implementation — not predicted.

## Current code facts (handoff §6 — verify before relying, may drift)

`mcp-agent/src/agent/agent.py`: hardcoded to Anthropic (`import anthropic`,
`MODEL="claude-sonnet-4-5"`, `MAX_TOKENS=1024` — this is the OUTPUT cap, not memory), a
`SYSTEM_PROMPT` constant, `run_query(client, user_input, messages) -> (final_text, messages)`,
and `interactive_mode` REPL that persists `messages` across turns (follow-ups work in REPL;
single-shot `--query` does not persist). `mcp-agent/src/agent/tools.py` holds tool defs +
`execute_tool`. No observability anywhere yet — clean slate. `claims-agent` has a `--no-llm`
deterministic mode usable as a live oracle for drift detection.

## Related memories flagged as relevant (handoff §10)

[[llm-tool-schema-oneof-unreliable]] — directly relevant to M1 and M5 (flatten tool schemas,
validate cross-field rules downstream; expect worse behavior from small self-hosted models).
[[pytest-test-filename-collision]] — check before adding any new test file.
[[secret-values-never-print]] — extends naturally to PHI redaction in traces/logs (topic 3).

## Suggested first move (handoff §12)

Confirm §8 open questions with user → draft `docs/phase5/plan.md` + `docs/phase5/README.md` on a
`docs/phase5-*` branch (planning only) → open docs PR → then start M1 (enum gate) as first
implementation PR.

# mcp-agent Investigation Report

Full file inventory (`mcp-agent/`): `pyproject.toml`, `README.md`, `Dockerfile`, `src/agent/__init__.py` (empty), `src/agent/agent.py` (269 lines), `src/agent/tools.py` (236 lines), `src/agent/format.py` (90 lines), `tests/__init__.py` (empty), `tests/test_e2e_demo_flow.py` (304 lines). That is the entire package — no `conftest.py`, no config file, no logging module, no observability module, no session-storage module.

## 1. Verification of handoff claims

- **`import anthropic`, `MODEL="claude-sonnet-4-5"`, `MAX_TOKENS=1024`** — CONFIRMED, `mcp-agent/src/agent/agent.py:33,47-48`:
  ```
  33  import anthropic
  ...
  47  MODEL = "claude-sonnet-4-5"
  48  MAX_TOKENS = 1024
  ```

- **`SYSTEM_PROMPT` constant** — CONFIRMED, `agent.py:50-65`, a multi-line string defining the clinical-assistant persona (mandates calling `get_patient_summary` before `assess_refill_risk`, mandates including risk level/rationale/RiskAssessment ID/recommendation, instructs to be "direct and emphatic" on HIGH risk, and "never fabricate patient data").

- **`run_query(client, user_input, messages) -> (final_text, messages)`** — CONFIRMED, `agent.py:72-139`. Actual signature is `run_query(client, user_input, messages=None, verbose=True) -> tuple[str, list[dict]]`, so the handoff's description is accurate but incomplete — it omits the `verbose` parameter. It loops on `response.stop_reason == "tool_use"`, calling `execute_tool` for every tool_use block and feeding results back, until a non-tool_use response, then returns `(final_text, messages)`.

- **`interactive_mode` REPL persists `messages`; `--query` does NOT persist** — CONFIRMED.
  - `interactive_mode` (`agent.py:205-231`): initializes `messages: list[dict] = []` once outside the `while True:` loop (line 208) and reassigns it each turn via `final_text, messages = run_query(client, user_input, messages)` (line 225) — so conversation state persists across REPL turns.
  - `non_interactive_mode` (`agent.py:234-246`): calls `run_query(client, query)` with no `messages` argument (line 238), and the process exits after one query (`main()` → `sys.exit(non_interactive_mode(...))`, lines 262-263). Each `--query` invocation is a fresh process with empty history — confirmed no persistence across invocations (and there's no on-disk session store to persist to — see item 5).

- **`tools.py` holds tool definitions + `execute_tool`** — CONFIRMED. `TOOL_DEFINITIONS` list at `tools.py:29-81`, dispatcher `execute_tool(name, inputs) -> str` at `tools.py:221-236`.

- **No observability (no OTel/metrics/tracing) anywhere in mcp-agent** — CONFIRMED. Grep for `opentelemetry|otel|prometheus|statsd|datadog|jaeger|tracing|metrics|logging.getLogger|logger =|structlog` across `mcp-agent/` returned zero hits. The only "instrumentation" is `print()`-based console output for tool calls/results (`_print_tool_call`/`_print_tool_result`, `agent.py:142-175`) and formatted terminal strings in `format.py` — purely for interactive/demo display, not logs or metrics.

## 2. Tool schemas

Two tools, both defined in `mcp-agent/src/agent/tools.py:29-81`:

1. **`get_patient_summary`** (`tools.py:31-49`)
   - `input_schema.properties`: `name` (string, required) — "Patient name or partial name to search for."
   - `required: ["name"]`
   - Flat, single string param. No nesting.

2. **`assess_refill_risk`** (`tools.py:50-80`)
   - `input_schema.properties`: `patient_id` (string, required), `medication_id` (string, optional)
   - `required: ["patient_id"]`
   - Flat, two string params. No nesting.

**No `oneOf`, `anyOf`, `allOf`, nested objects, arrays, or enum types appear anywhere in the tool `input_schema`s.** Both schemas are as simple/robust as JSON-schema for tool-calling gets — flat objects with only string properties. This is a mitigating fact, not a risk, for any "fragile schema" critique in the handoff — there's nothing schema-fragile here to harden.

**Enum-typed *output* fields already in use (not input schemas, but worth flagging since the handoff-relevant risk area is agent output validation):**
- Risk level is an informal string enum `HIGH | MODERATE | LOW` (plus a fallback `"UNKNOWN"`) threaded through several places:
  - `tools.py:197-202` extracts `risk_code` from the triage service's FHIR `RiskAssessment.prediction[0].outcome.coding[0].code`, defaulting to the literal string `"UNKNOWN"` if any key is missing (via chained `.get(..., {})` / `.get(..., [{}])[0]` calls — fails silently to `"UNKNOWN"` rather than erroring).
  - `format.py:10-14` (`RISK_ICONS`) and `format.py:16-20` (`RISK_LABELS`) are dicts keyed on `"HIGH"/"MODERATE"/"LOW"` with `.get(risk_level, "❓")` / `.get(risk_level, f"{risk_level} RISK")` fallbacks for unrecognized values — so an unknown code degrades gracefully to a generic label rather than crashing, but there is **no schema/enum constraint enforced anywhere** (no Python `Enum`, no Pydantic model, no JSON-schema `enum` list) — it's all string comparison by convention.

## 3. Error handling / safety today

- **FHIR-service errors**: `get_patient_summary` catches `FHIRClientError` and `RuntimeError` (missing `FHIR_GATEWAY_URL`) and returns `{"error": "..."}` dicts (`tools.py:118-121`) rather than raising — these get serialized to JSON and handed back to Claude as a tool_result, so the LLM sees the error as text and must decide how to respond. No retry, no backoff, no circuit breaker.
- **Triage-service errors**: `assess_refill_risk` catches `httpx.HTTPStatusError` (extracts `detail` from the JSON error body if present) and `httpx.RequestError` (network-level failure, e.g. service down) and again returns `{"error": "..."}` dicts (`tools.py:184-194`) rather than raising. Same pattern — no retry/backoff/timeout-retry logic; there is a flat 30-second `httpx.post(..., timeout=30.0)` (`tools.py:180`) but no configurable per-call timeout, no circuit breaker.
- **Malformed/unexpected triage response shape**: the field-extraction at `tools.py:197-205` uses defensive chained `.get()` with `{}` / `[{}]` defaults, so a malformed response degrades to `risk_code = "UNKNOWN"` rather than throwing a `KeyError`/`IndexError` — this is effectively **fail-open at the parsing layer** (an unparseable/malformed response is silently treated as an "UNKNOWN" risk string handed to the LLM as ordinary text, not surfaced as an error or blocked). There is no code path that refuses to answer or forces a "cannot verify" response when the risk parsing fails this way.
- **Ambiguous patient lookups**: `get_patient_summary` distinguishes not-found (`found: False` + suggestion message, `tools.py:123-128`) from multiple-matches (`found: True, multiple_matches: True, count, patients[], message` asking for clarification, `tools.py:140-155`). This is structured data the LLM is *expected* to use to ask the clinician to disambiguate (per `SYSTEM_PROMPT`'s "if you cannot find a patient, say so clearly"), but **nothing programmatically prevents** the LLM from picking one of several matches and proceeding to call `assess_refill_risk` anyway — there's no code-level guard forcing disambiguation.
- **Top-level exception handling**: both `interactive_mode` (`agent.py:224-231`) and `non_interactive_mode` (`agent.py:237-246`) wrap `run_query` in `try/except anthropic.APIError` (prints a formatted error) and a bare `except Exception` (prints error). Notably, `interactive_mode`'s bare-`Exception` handler **re-raises after printing** (`agent.py:229-231`, `raise` on the line after the error print) — meaning an unexpected exception crashes the whole REPL process; `non_interactive_mode`'s equivalent handler does not re-raise, just returns exit code 1 (`agent.py:244-246`). This asymmetry (crash-on-exception in interactive mode, graceful-exit in `--query` mode) is worth flagging as inconsistent behavior.
- **Validation of the LLM's final answer**: **None.** `run_query` returns `final_text` built by simply concatenating every `block.text` from the model's final (non-tool-use) response content (`agent.py:130-133`), and both entry points just `print(agent_response(final_text))` (`agent.py:226,239`) with zero post-hoc validation — no check that risk level/assessment ID were actually included, no regex/schema validation of the narrative, no guard against the model contradicting the tool output or hallucinating a risk level not returned by the triage service. The `SYSTEM_PROMPT` *instructs* the model to always include patient name/risk level/rationale/assessment ID (lines 57-61) and to never fabricate data (line 65), but this is prompt-only guidance — nothing in code enforces or checks it. This is a legitimate, real gap for a "hardening" phase to target.
- **Fail-open vs fail-closed**: overall the system is **fail-open** — every error path (FHIR down, triage down, malformed response, unknown risk code) degrades to returning descriptive text/JSON that gets handed to the LLM to narrate, rather than any code path that blocks/refuses output or requires a human override. There is no mechanism that prevents the agent from producing a "dispense" recommendation in the presence of a tool/service failure — nothing hard-stops output when `{"error": ...}` payloads are seen; it's entirely up to the LLM's own judgment per the system prompt.

## 4. Tests

# Investigation Report: Phase 5 Plan Claims vs. Repo Reality

## 1. `claims-agent/` architecture

**Confirmed: it is a non-authoritative explanation agent.** From `/workspaces/fhir-agent/claims-agent/README.md` (lines 1-6) and `claims-agent/src/claims_agent/agent.py` (lines 3-8, 44-45):

> "It is **non-authoritative** (R17.8) — it calls the claims-service to obtain the *authoritative* decision and only narrates it; it never computes, changes, or overrides an outcome."

The system prompt explicitly instructs: *"You must NEVER change, override, or contradict the decision the tool returns — you only narrate it. Never invent reasons, amounts, or outcomes."* The single tool, `adjudicate_claim` (`claims-agent/src/claims_agent/tools.py`), POSTs to `claims-service` `/claims/adjudicate` and returns whatever it gets back — no local business logic exists in the package. This confirms the plan's characterization.

**LLM/provider:** Same as `mcp-agent` — raw **Anthropic SDK** (`anthropic>=0.28`), hardcoded model `claude-sonnet-4-5`, no framework/abstraction layer (`claims-agent/src/claims_agent/agent.py:31-33,99-104`). No provider abstraction exists in either agent — both instantiate `anthropic.Anthropic(...)` directly and hardcode the model string.

**Deterministic `--no-llm` oracle: confirmed.** `claims-agent/src/claims_agent/agent.py` has `--no-llm` (line 117) and falls back automatically when no API key is set (`__main__`/`agent.py` lines 130-133). The deterministic path uses `explain.py`'s `render_explanation()` — a template renderer requiring no API key, used both standalone and as "the grounding the LLM elaborates when one is [available]" (`explain.py` line 6-7). This is a genuinely useful oracle/reference implementation absent from `mcp-agent` (which has no deterministic/no-LLM mode — it hard-requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, see `mcp-agent/src/agent/agent.py:182-192`).

**Shape vs. `mcp-agent`:** Nearly identical skeleton — both are raw Anthropic tool-use loops with a `SYSTEM_PROMPT`, a `TOOL_DEFINITIONS` list, an `execute_tool` dispatcher, and a `format.py` for terminal output. Differences:
- `claims-agent` is single-shot (`explain_claim()` — one claim in, one explanation out); `mcp-agent` has a stateful interactive REPL (`interactive_mode`) that accumulates `messages` across turns — i.e., `mcp-agent` has *more* conversational/session machinery, not less.
- `claims-agent` has a deterministic mode; `mcp-agent` does not.
- Neither has persisted memory/session storage (both just hold `messages` in a Python list for process lifetime), and **neither has any observability/tracing instrumentation** (no OTel, no structured logging beyond print statements, in either agent).

So: no provider abstraction, no durable memory, no observability exists in *either* agent — the plan's premise that `claims-agent` might already have infrastructure `mcp-agent` lacks (or vice versa) is **not supported**; they're both minimal/equivalent in that respect except for the deterministic-mode oracle in `claims-agent`.

## 2. Phase 2 completion status

`docs/phase2/README.md` lines 3-5 (the explicitly-declared "one canonical status statement"):

> **"BUILT and running locally (M0–M7 complete)."** ... **"Not deployed to cloud (M8 / Phase 2b not started)."**

`docs/phase2/plan.md` §6 milestone table (lines 275-283): **M0 through M7 are all marked `✅ Done`**; **M8 = Phase 2b is `⏳ Not started`**. So Phase 2 (as scoped, excluding the separately-tracked M8/live-cloud-deploy) is documented as complete. This is accurate reporting, not "done"-washing — the docs are explicit that M8 (live cloud) remains outstanding and is treated as a distinct deliverable.

## 3. "Cloud-delivery-gap" claim

**Accurate — well documented**, in `docs/phase2/plan.md` §6, in a callout box titled exactly **"⚠️ Cloud-delivery gap"** (lines 289-310):

> "**What does not exist, despite being implied above:** `infra/terraform/` — the top-level root module ... M0's 'Terraform skeleton' touchpoint was never delivered. `deploy-phase2.sh`. Any Cloud Run config for `claims-agent` ... Any executed cloud smoke test..."
>
> "**Consequence:** Phase 2b is **not** 'terraform apply, not new construction'. There is no root module to apply — the per-service stubs are unreferenced fragments. Real authoring work remains, tracked as §16 item 9a."

Verified against the tree: `claims-service/infra/main.tf` and `rxclaim-emulator/infra/main.tf` exist (per-service Cloud Run stubs, confirmed via directory listing), but `infra/terraform/` and `deploy-phase2.sh` do **not** exist anywhere in the repo. `docs/phase2/decisions.md` D8 corroborates: *"⚠️ Partially delivered ... Per-service Cloud Run stubs shipped for the two Java services (M2, M3); the top-level root module, deploy-phase2.sh, claims-agent's config, and the cloud smoke test never did."* **The plan's claim is accurate and directly quotable from the repo's own docs.**

## 4. R15 claim

R15 = "Observability" (`docs/phase2/requirements.md:172-180`): distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry → Cloud Trace, one claim = one trace), metrics (Micrometer/Prometheus → Google Managed Prometheus), and correlation IDs in PHI-scrubbed logs.

The milestone table (`plan.md:278`) claims M3's cloud touchpoint was **"OTel tracing wired"** and marks M3 `✅ Done`. **I checked the actual code and this claim does not hold up**: `claims-service/pom.xml` and `rxclaim-emulator/pom.xml` contain `spring-boot-starter-actuator` (health/readiness only) but **no `micrometer` or `opentelemetry` dependency at all**. `grep` for `MDC`, `traceId`, `X-Correlation`, `X-Trace` across `claims-service/src`, `rxclaim-emulator/src`, `claims-agent/src` returned nothing; the only hits for "trace" in the Java sources are unrelated uses of the word ("audit/trace" in docstrings, `ClaimIntakeContractTest`), not distributed-tracing code. The only real observability artifact in the repo is Kong's Prometheus plugin (`gateway/kong/kong-plugins.yaml`, `kong-values.yaml`) — gateway-level request metrics on **Phase 1's** GKE Kong, not per-service business/tracing instrumentation.

Notably, `docs/testing-guide.md` §4 ("What is not tested — known gaps") and `docs/phase2/decisions.md`'s "Partially delivered" list (D8, C1, C2, C3) **never call out an R15/observability gap explicitly** — despite the milestone table asserting it's done. This is itself a documentation-vs-code discrepancy the repo's own review process hasn't caught yet.

**Verdict on the plan's R15 claim:** plausible and arguably *understated by the repo's own docs* — code evidence indicates R15 (tracing/metrics/correlation IDs) is substantially unbuilt at the service level, more unbuilt than the milestone table's "Done"/"OTel tracing wired" language admits. The plan's claim that Phase 5's observability slice "may legitimately close" R15 is well-founded, though it's worth noting this isn't a claim the repo documents anywhere as an open gap the way the cloud-delivery-gap is — it's something I found by reading code, not something Phase 2's docs themselves flag.

## 5. Status-truthfulness problem — confirmed, with an important refinement on "tagged"

Commit `0fcc196` — `docs: resolve review findings — status truth, safety semantics, gateway runbook, ADR index` (author: Bhaskar Srinivasan, `bhaskar.cmu@gmail.com`) — is exactly this incident:

> "Addresses eight review findings. The theme is truthfulness: several documents asserted things the repository does not support.
>
> **Critical — status conflict.** plan.md's header still said 'No application code exists yet' while README.md and plan §6 said M0-M7 are complete. Status is now stated ONCE, canonically, in docs/phase2/README.md..."
>
> "**High — cloud artifacts claimed but absent.** The plan implied 'by M7 the cloud path is fully authored; Phase 2b is terraform apply'. Reality: per-service Cloud Run stubs exist... but there is NO root module, no deploy-phase2.sh, no claims-agent config, and no cloud smoke test."

This is precisely the reviewer-caught status-inflation incident the plan references, and it directly produced the cloud-delivery-gap callout (item 3) and the canonical single-status-statement convention (item 2).

**However — one part of the plan's framing is not accurate:** the plan describes Phase 2 as "**tagged**." I checked git tags directly (`git tag -l -n99`): the repo has exactly **one** tag, `phase1-v1`, whose message states it is *"a known-good, independently runnable and cloud-tested snapshot taken **before** Phase 2 ... work begins."* There is **no Phase 2 tag** (e.g. no `phase2-v1`). Phase 2's "done" status lives only in prose (`docs/phase2/README.md`'s canonical statement), not in a git tag. **This is a factual error in the plan** if it's asserting Phase 2 itself was tagged — only Phase 1 has ever been tagged in this repo.

## 6. `claims-service` and `rxclaim-emulator`

- **`claims-service`** (`claims-service/README.md:1-6`) — the modern Java/Spring Boot **API façade** over the legacy core. Runs the layered benefit/prior-auth rules engine and the Decision Contract (R17), reuses the Python `triage-service` for clinical safety, and talks to `rxclaim-emulator` through an anti-corruption layer. This is the *authoritative* decision-maker.
- **`rxclaim-emulator`** (`rxclaim-emulator/README.md:1-9`) — a Spring Boot service simulating the legacy IBM i / RxClaim adjudication core (DDS-style fixed-width records, DB2/SQL400-style tables, an `ADJRXCLM` RPG/CL-flavored function). It owns the member system-of-record, pricing, and accumulators; `claims-service` wraps it and consumers never call it directly.
- **`claims-agent`** sits on top of `claims-service` only — it POSTs a claim to `claims-service`'s `/claims/adjudicate` and narrates whatever `claims-service` (which itself may have called `rxclaim-emulator` and `triage-service`) decided. `claims-agent` has no direct relationship to `rxclaim-emulator`.

---

### Summary of flags for the critique

- **Items 1–4 check out** against the repo's own docs and code, with one enhancement worth adding to the critique: R15's "unbuilt" status is *even more true* than the plan states — actual code inspection (no Micrometer/OpenTelemetry dependency, no correlation-ID/MDC code) shows the milestone table's "OTel tracing wired" (M3) claim is itself inflated, and this specific gap isn't named anywhere in `decisions.md`'s partial-delivery list or `testing-guide.md`'s known-gaps list, unlike the cloud-delivery gap.
- **Item 5 is confirmed** as a real, well-documented incident (commit `0fcc196`), but the plan's word **"tagged"** applied to Phase 2 is **inaccurate** — only Phase 1 (`phase1-v1`) has a git tag in this repo; Phase 2 has no tag at all, only a prose "canonical status" statement in `docs/phase2/README.md`. If the critique repeats "tagged" uncritically it will be repeating an error.

Repo root: /workspaces/fhir-agent. I'm preparing a critique of a "Phase 5: Agent Platform Hardening" plan for a Python LLM agent (`mcp-agent/`) in this healthcare (FHIR/PHI) repo. The plan wants to add: rate/cost-limiting (a client-side token-bucket in front of the paid LLM API, with alerts not auto-shed, "clinical — never silently drop a care request"), fail-closed output validation, and PHI redaction in observability. I want to know what conventions already exist elsewhere in the deterministic tiers of this repo (`triage-service/`, `fhir-service/`, `claims-service/`, `gateway/`) so any new agent-tier work is consistent with, not reinventing, existing patterns.

Please investigate and report on:

1. **`triage-service/src/triage/rules.py`**: What does the actual drug-allergy risk rule engine look like? How does it represent risk levels (HIGH/MODERATE/LOW/UNKNOWN)? Is there an existing "fail-closed" convention here (e.g., unrecognized/ambiguous input maps to a conservative/high-risk outcome rather than silently passing)? Quote the relevant logic.

2. **PHI handling conventions**: Search the repo for how PHI is currently handled/protected/redacted anywhere (logs, error messages, test fixtures, docs). Is there a documented PHI policy? Any existing redaction code or logging wrapper?

3. **Gateway (Kong) rate limiting**: Read `gateway/` config. What rate limiting exists today (which services, what limits, key-auth setup)? Is it "fail closed" (block over limit) or does it degrade some other way? This is relevant baseline for the plan's proposed client-side token-bucket for the LLM API call.

4. **Kong / infra observability**: Does the Kong gateway config include any Prometheus plugin or metrics export already? (Cross-check with what another agent may have found — just report what you see in `gateway/`.)

5. **fhir-service and claims-service error-shape conventions**: The commit log mentions "error shape" as one of Phase 4's "three quirks." What's the documented/actual error response shape convention across services? Is there a consistent pattern (e.g. HTTP status codes, structured error body) that an agent-tier fail-closed REVIEW outcome should mirror for consistency?

6. **Any existing queue/deadline/timeout patterns**: grep for `deadline`, `timeout`, `Queue`, `asyncio.wait_for`, `circuit.?breaker` across triage-service, claims-service, fhir-service, gateway. Report what request-timeout/resilience conventions already exist in the deterministic tier that the agent tier should match.

Report factually, organized by these 6 numbered items, with file paths, line numbers, and direct quotes/code snippets. This is research only — do not modify any files.

lastPrompt: Now critique everything, analyze what has been implemented and documented in the codebase to confirm what you need to learn about past work, and tell me what is clear and what we need to discuss. Do n…

# Investigation Report: Phase 5 "Agent Platform Hardening" Plan — Verification Against Existing Docs/Infra

## 1. `docs/phase5/` contents

**Only one file exists**: `/workspaces/fhir-agent/docs/phase5/phase4-testing-and-analysis.md`. There is no `readiness-assessment.md`, no PRD, no scope/milestone doc for "agent platform hardening" anywhere in `docs/phase5/`.

The current branch is `docs/phase5-readiness-assessment`, but the only file present is titled **"Phase 4 Testing & Analysis — Input to Defining Phase 5"**, and its header states plainly:

> "**Status:** DRAFT — a testing/analysis exercise performed after Phase 4 (M1–M5) was complete and merged, **not a Phase 5 PRD itself**." (line 3-4)

**What it actually assesses readiness for**: whether the already-merged Phase 4 (`epic-emulator`) is safe/valuable/well-built enough to demo or build on — not agent platform readiness, not memory/observability/multi-provider/output-safety.

**Headline finding (§0, lines 13-34)**: a live, unfixed clinical-safety bug — `epic-emulator`'s pagination cap (20 records) combined with `client/clinical`'s FHIR client never following `Bundle.link[relation=next]` causes a silent false-negative on drug-allergy conflict checks for patients with >20 allergy records. Table shows 22/22 allergies via `fhir-service` directly vs. only 20/22 (missing the penicillin allergy) via `epic-emulator`, flipping the triage result from **HIGH** ("CONFLICT DETECTED... Do not dispense") to **LOW** ("Safe to dispense").

**Scope/topics it does propose for Phase 5 (§4, lines 192-245)**:
- 4.0: Fix or mitigate the pagination bug *before* Phase 5 starts — "This is a live safety-relevant bug in merged code, not a Phase 5 backlog item."
- 4.1: Add "consequence-level" tests (realistic data volume, not just shape) for any quirk/backfill that changes response content.
- 4.2: Wire `epic-emulator` into CI (`phase4-java` job mirroring `phase2-java`/`phase3`).
- 4.3: **Decompose auth first** if/when Phase 5 decomposes `epic-emulator` at all (per the coupling note) — extension handling and pagination should stay together; error-shape formatting needs "an explicit home."
- 4.4: Resolve decision E10 (unverified Epic placeholder values) if real Epic sandbox access ever becomes available.
- 4.5: Update `docs/demo-guide.md` for Phase 4, once §4.0 is resolved.

**Conflict with the "agent platform hardening" framing**: this document's entire content is about `epic-emulator` (Epic EHR integration quirks, pagination, auth, extensions) and its coupling/decomposition — it contains **zero mentions** of `mcp-agent`, memory, observability, multi-provider LLM support, or output-safety milestones. A plan that frames "Phase 5" as agent-platform-hardening piloted on `mcp-agent` is not built on this document's proposed scope; it appears to substitute a different subject matter under the same phase number. `docs/phase4/README.md` (lines 56-57) makes the pre-existing framing explicit: **"A future Phase 5 would decompose along whatever the coupling note actually shows, not the original three-area guess... No Phase 5 work has started; no timeline set."**

## 2. Phase 4 status

Files: `docs/phase4/README.md`, `prd.md`, `design.md`, `decisions.md`, `coupling-note.md`.

`docs/phase4/README.md` is explicit that this is "the one canonical status statement" (line 35). Key facts:

- **Scope confirmed** (lines 59-88): `epic-emulator` = (1) SMART Backend Services JWT auth emulation, (2) Epic custom extensions backfill on Medication/AllergyIntolerance, (3) "three named quirks — pagination cap + opaque continuation, the required-search-parameter rejection, and Epic-shaped `OperationOutcome` errors."
- **Completion status**: "**Phase 4 milestones: complete — M1 through M5 all built.**" (line 11) — 24 unit/integration tests, M5's acceptance case verified live via `e2e/test_epic_emulator_acceptance.py`.
- **But NOT fully closed**: The top of the file has a warning banner (lines 3-9): "**⚠️ All 5 milestones are built and merged, but a post-merge safety finding is still open**... Not yet fixed." And later (lines 50-57): "**What's next:** Phase 4 is built and merged, but **not fully closed**."
- **Explicitly deferred/loose ends relevant to agent hardening**: None — Phase 4's deferred items are Epic-specific (M2's Epic-doc-version pinning is "still only partially done," decision E10 flags unverified placeholder values, `athena-emulator/` remains an untouched placeholder). Nothing in Phase 4 touches `mcp-agent`, LLM providers, memory, or observability.
- **Terminology note** (lines 83-88): "Phase" is reserved for top-level phases — Phase 1-4 plus "a possible future **Phase 4b**" (live cloud deployment) — no mention of agent hardening anywhere in this doc.

## 3. `docs/README.md` — documented phase roadmap

Read in full (`docs/README.md`). The documented phase structure is:

- **Phase 2** — claims-adjudication modernization (`docs/phase2/`), with **Phase 2b** as "the future live-deployment phase" (line 104).
- **Phase 3** — Provider Search & Referral, "M1–M7 complete; **Phase 3b** (live cloud deployment) not started" (line 60).
- **Phase 4** — Epic Emulator, "Milestones complete, one safety finding open" (line 71).
- **Phase 5** — described only as (lines 87-91): "**not a phase yet, just one document**: a clinician/business-stakeholder/architect testing-and-analysis pass over completed Phase 4, done against real running services. Leads with a live, unresolved safety bug (§0)... plus recommendations for whatever Phase 5 becomes."

**No mention of "Phase 6" anywhere** in `docs/README.md` (confirmed via grep — only "Phase 5" appears, 3 times, all referring to the epic-emulator-decomposition-input document above). There is no documented scope for Phase 5 as agent-platform-hardening, and nothing reserves "Phase 6" for that either. Given the explicit "Phase 4b"/"Phase 2b"/"Phase 3b" numbering convention already established (sub-letter for live-deployment follow-ons to a completed phase), a plan asking "should this be Phase 5 or Phase 6" is choosing between two numbers neither of which the existing docs assign to agent hardening — the docs' own next open slot for "Phase 5" is already spoken for by epic-emulator decomposition work per the coupling note, not agent hardening.

## 4. Existing observability/gateway infra — repo-wide

**This is NOT a clean slate.** Contrary to a plan assuming Phase 5 M2/M4 (observability) starts from scratch:

**Already declared/built:**
- **Kong gateway (`gateway/kong/kong-plugins.yaml`, lines 99-125)**: A `KongClusterPlugin` named `fhir-prometheus` is defined and applied globally, exposing Kong's built-in Prometheus metrics endpoint on port 8100 with `status_code_metrics`, `latency_metrics`, `bandwidth_metrics`, `upstream_health_metrics` all `true`.
- **`gateway/kong/kong-values.yaml`** (lines 159-190): A full `serviceMonitor` block (Prometheus Operator CRD) configured for GKE Managed Prometheus, 30s scrape interval, documented as auto-activating when Managed Prometheus is enabled in GKE console (currently declared but "not scraped" until that's turned on — `gateway/README.md` line 468-469).
- **Rate limiting already configured** (`kong-plugins.yaml` lines 34-73): `fhir-rate-limit` plugin — 10 req/s, 1000/day per consumer, `policy: cluster` (writes to Neon Postgres so usage is queryable via SQL), documented upgrade path to Redis at scale.
- **Structured request logging**: `fhir-request-log` global `file-log` plugin to stdout, captured by GKE Cloud Logging.
- **`fhir-service`** (HAPI FHIR / Spring Boot): `pom.xml` has `micrometer-core`, `micrometer-registry-prometheus`, `micrometer-registry-prometheus-simpleclient` dependencies (v1.16.2), and `application.yaml`/`application-cds.yaml` have Spring Actuator's `prometheus` endpoint enabled (`management.endpoint.prometheus.enabled: true`).
- **Phase 2 docs already fully specify an OTel + Prometheus design** — `docs/phase2/plan.md` (lines 253-254, 278-283, 485) and `docs/phase2/requirements.md` (lines 174-177): "Tracing → OpenTelemetry (`traceparent`) across the fan-out → Cloud Trace; metrics → Managed Prometheus (per-stage latency + approvals/denials/pends/rule-fires)." M3/M4 in the Phase 2 plan table are marked "✅ Done" with "OTel tracing wired."

**What's NOT actually present (aspirational/docs-only, not code):**
- A repo-wide grep for `opentelemetry`/`traceparent` in actual source (`*.py`, `*.java`, `*.ts`, `*.js`) returned **zero matches** — no OTel SDK is actually imported/wired into any service despite the Phase 2 docs claiming "OTel tracing wired" for M3/M4.
- No `requirements.txt`/`pyproject.toml`/`package.json` anywhere references `opentelemetry` or `prometheus` as a dependency (confirmed by grep across the whole repo) — the micrometer/Prometheus deps found are Java/`fhir-service` (HAPI-starter) only, Python services (`triage-service`, `claims-service` is Java actually, `mcp-agent`) have no metrics libraries.
- No Grafana, Jaeger anywhere in the repo (grep returned zero hits for those terms outside the general search list, i.e., they didn't even appear as candidate files).
- `mcp-agent/` itself (`mcp-agent/README.md`, `pyproject.toml`, `Dockerfile`, one test file) has **no observability code at all** — it's a minimal Anthropic-tool-use-API script with no framework, no instrumentation.

**Bottom line for the critique**: Phase 5 M2/M4 would not be starting from a clean slate at the *platform edge* (Kong Prometheus + rate-limiting is live infrastructure, already deployed and documented), but it would be starting from a clean slate for *application-level/LLM tracing* (no OTel SDK anywhere in code, despite Phase 2 docs asserting it's "wired"). A plan claiming "no existing observability infra" is wrong about the gateway; a plan claiming "OTel is already wired per Phase 2" (per the docs) would be repeating a documentation claim that doesn't match the actual code.

## 5. Existing `policy.md` / fail-closed / output-safety conventions

**No `policy.md` file exists anywhere in the repo** (searched by filename, zero results).

**A fail-closed convention is already established and load-bearing**, in `claims-service`, not invented fresh:

- **`claims-service/src/main/java/com/payer/claims/domain/Severity.java`** (full file, 12 lines):
```java
public enum Severity {
    DENY,    // hard denial
    PEND,    // needs PA / more info
    REVIEW,  // route to manual review
    INFO     // annotation only; never changes the outcome
}
```
- **`claims-service/src/main/java/com/payer/claims/domain/Outcome.java`**:
```java
public enum Outcome {
    APPROVED,
    DENIED,
    PENDED,
    ROUTED_FOR_REVIEW
}
```
- **The fail-closed rule itself**, `claims-service/src/main/java/com/payer/claims/rules/RulesEngine.java` line 74-78:
```java
} else if (risk == RiskLevel.UNKNOWN) {
    // Fail closed: an incomplete safety check must not silently approve. A human decides.
    f.add(Finding.of("CLINICAL-SAFETY-UNAVAILABLE", "clinical", Severity.PEND,
            "clinical-safety-unavailable",
            "Clinical-safety check could not be completed; pharmacist review required."));
}
```
- **`docs/testing-guide.md`** (lines 365-368) documents this as a deliberate, hard-won design decision: *"A fail-closed contract. `LOW` meant both 'safe' and 'unknown'. Once those are the same value, no test can tell them apart... → now `RiskLevel.UNKNOWN` → PEND."* And the transferable lesson (line 376): **"Make 'I don't know' a distinct value. If unavailable and safe share a representation, no amount of testing recovers the difference."**
- This convention is reused/referenced across `docs/phase2/decisions.md` (D1), `docs/phase2/plan.md` (lines 528, 547 — circuit breaker "preserving the fail-closed policy"), `claims-service/README.md` (lines 65, 101, 122), and `docs/demo-guide.md` (line 271 — "CI doesn't run e2e. That's how a fail-closed regression reached `main`").

**`REVIEW` is already a first-class status value** in the platform's decision vocabulary (`Severity.REVIEW`, `Outcome.ROUTED_FOR_REVIEW`), tied to a specific meaning — "route to manual review" — as distinct from `PEND` ("needs PA/more info, safety-check-unavailable") and `DENY` (hard denial).

**Implication for Phase 5's output-safety milestone (M1)**: there is a specific, tested, documented convention already in force — three/four-tier severity (DENY/PEND/REVIEW/INFO), "unknown ≠ safe" as a distinct fail-closed state, and "REVIEW" specifically meaning human-review-routing rather than a generic catch-all. If Phase 5's M1 proposes its own status vocabulary (e.g., a binary allow/block, or reusing "REVIEW" to mean something else) without reconciling it against `claims-service`'s `Severity`/`Outcome` enums and the `RiskLevel.UNKNOWN → PEND` precedent, it would be inventing a parallel convention rather than extending the one the codebase already treats as load-bearing and cites in its own testing-guide "coda" as the top lesson learned.

Fails closed. Treating 'we could not check' as 'we checked and it is safe' lets a claim approve on a safety check that never ran; the failure is silent, because a system that cannot see a drug-allergy conflict reports no conflict. So an incomplete check pends for a human rather than approving." `RiskLevel.UNKNOWN ⇒ PEND` (never approve; a hard `DENY` still outranks it per R17.3). PHI handling conventions There is a documented policy (`docs/phase2/requirements.md` **R14** — "Security & privacy (treat claims data as if PHI)") and **R15** (Observability), plus at least one real implementation and one real regression: - **R14** (`docs/phase2/requirements.md:157`): "PHI-safe logging: do not emit patient/member identifiers to logs... scrub identifiers or treat those logs as a restricted PHI store." - **R15** (`docs/phase2/requirements.md:172`): "Correlation IDs in PHI-scrubbed structured logs" — i.e., the convention is to log a `decisionId`/correlation id, never the member/patient id (also stated in `docs/phase2/plan.md:483`: "log `decisionId`, not member id"). - **Java claims-service** enforces this at the error-response layer too: `ClaimValidationAdvice.java` deliberately does *not* echo parser error detail back to the caller because "claims are treated as PHI (R14)." **Concrete redaction implementation** — `provider-registry-service/src/provider_registry/location.py`, function `sanitize_location()`: ```python def sanitize_location(zip: str | None, lat: float | None, lon: float | None) -> str: """PHI-safe location summary for logs (design.md §11/§12.1): never log the raw ZIP or exact coordinate a caller searched from — bucket to a 3-digit ZIP prefix or a whole-degree region instead.""" if zip: return f"zip3:{zip[:3]}" if lat is not None and lon is not None: return f"region:{round(lat)},{round(lon)}" return "unknown" ``` Paired with `provider-registry-service/src/provider_registry/logging_middleware.py`, whose docstring states the design principle explicitly: > "Deliberately structural, not scrub-after-the-fact: this middleware logs only method, path, status code, and duration — it never reads the request body, so it cannot leak a raw search location into logs regardless of whether a call site remembers to sanitize." **A documented near-miss is directly relevant to the plan's PHI-in-observability item.** `docs/developer-guide.md:335-342`: > "A design doc can name an enforcement mechanism that was never actually wired in. `design.md` §12.1 described a `sanitize_location()` helper and a request-logging middleware enforcing PHI-safe location handling — for five milestones, before anyone checked `main.py` against the claim. It wasn't there; `RateLimitMiddleware` was the only middleware that existed... The general lesson: 'Fixed here' in a design doc describes an intent until something in the codebase actually points back at it — treat a security-relevant claim with no corresponding file/line reference as unverified, not as done." **A live, currently-unfixed PHI exposure exists in the gateway today** — `docs/gateway-runbook.md:248-250`: > "**PHI in gateway logs (⚠️ applies to Phase 1 today).** Kong's `file-log` records request URIs, which contain patient and member identifiers. Treat gateway logs as **restricted**, or scrub them (R14). This is a real, current exposure — not a Phase 2 concern." This confirms Kong's `fhir-request-log` plugin (`gateway/kong/kong-plugins.yaml:127-143`) writes raw `request.uri` (e.g. `/fhir/Patient/123`) to stdout — an acknowledged, still-open PHI gap that any new agent-tier observability work should not repeat. ## 3. Gateway (Kong) rate limiting There are **two separate Kong deployments** in this repo (per `gateway/README.md` and `docs/gateway-runbook.md`), and their rate-limiting posture differs: **Phase 1 (Kubernetes/Helm KIC, deployed today, fronts only `fhir-service`)** — `gateway/kong/kong-plugins.yaml`, `fhir-rate-limit` KongPlugin: ```yaml plugin: rate-limiting config: second: 10 # max 10 requests/sec (DoS/burst protection) day: 1000 # max 1000 requests/day (usage quota) policy: cluster # counters written to Neon (kongdb) on every request hide_client_headers: false error_code: 429 error_message: "API rate limit exceeded. It is also fail-closed/block-over-limit: ```python if len(hits) >= self._max_requests: return JSONResponse(status_code=429, content={"error_type": "rate_limited", "message": "too many requests"}) ``` This is the closest existing analog to the plan's proposed client-side token-bucket: an application-level (not gateway) rate limiter that hard-rejects (429) rather than degrading — but note it's a sliding-window counter, not a token bucket, and every existing rate limiter in this repo (gateway and in-process) **blocks/rejects over limit**; none of them "alert but don't shed." The plan's "alert not auto-shed" design for the LLM-call limiter would be a **new** pattern relative to every rate-limiting precedent in the repo, worth flagging explicitly as a deliberate departure, not an extension of existing convention — especially in tension with the "never silently drop a care request" framing, since "alert only" on a paid, clinical-tier API means requests still go through uncapped in practice. ## 4. Kong / infra observability — Prometheus Yes, Prometheus is already wired into the **Phase 1** Kong config. `gateway/kong/kong-plugins.yaml:99-126`, `fhir-prometheus` (`KongClusterPlugin`, global scope): ```yaml plugin: prometheus config: status_code_metrics: true latency_metrics: true bandwidth_metrics: true upstream_health_metrics: true ``` `gateway/README.md:367-386` documents the endpoint (`kong-kong-metrics:8100/metrics`) and states scraping depends on enabling GKE Managed Prometheus — the "Known Limitations" section is explicit: **"Prometheus metrics are declared but not scraped until Google Cloud Managed Prometheus is enabled in GKE.
